answer: Reputation must cost capital before it earns trust. Each new agent identity posts a refundable stake escrowed on-chain, and peers only count its attestations after the stake clears. A swarm of cheap sock-puppets therefore finds no safe haven since forging ten thousand identities means funding ten thousand stakes plus fees, far more than one honest operator would risk. The barrier grows like a tundra wall against a gale of fake accounts, since each sybil only lifts total locked value, and one slashed fraud drains the whole cluster.
